editionContext.scope: The story of Rostam and Esfandiar as the poem tells it: from Esfandiar’s claim to the crown and Goshtasp’s command to bring Rostam in bonds, through the meeting and fight on the Hirmand and the arrow of tamarisk, to Esfandiar’s iron coffin and Bahman’s return; the story of Rostam and Shaghad that follows is not part of it.
editionContext.evidencePolicy: Use actual verse for narrative assertions. Site-generated summaries are not the selected base text.
editionContext.translationPolicy: Original English paraphrases prepared for this collection; not a quoted modern translation.

Ganjoor, Ferdowsi’s Shahnameh: the table of contents

entities.label: The Shahnameh
entities.summary: The literary work in which the story of Rostam and Esfandiar is told.

entities.label: Ferdowsi
entities.summary: The poet of the Shahnameh.

entities.label: Rostam and Esfandiar
entities.summary: The story of how King Goshtasp sends his son Esfandiar to bring Rostam to court in bonds, and of the fight between the two champions on the Hirmand.

entities.label: Goshtasp
entities.summary: The king of Iran, father of Esfandiar, who has promised him the crown but, warned by Jamasp, sends him against Rostam instead.

entities.label: Esfandiar
entities.summary: The son of Goshtasp, champion of the faith, who has freed his father’s kingdom from Arjasp and now claims the crown.

entities.label: Katayun
entities.summary: The mother of Esfandiar, a daughter of the Caesar, who warns him against going to fight Rostam.

entities.label: Jamasp
entities.summary: The king’s sage and reader of the stars, who foretells that Esfandiar’s death lies in Zabulistan at the hand of Rostam.

entities.label: Peshotan
entities.summary: The brother and counsellor of Esfandiar, who urges peace with Rostam to the end and afterwards reproaches Goshtasp.

entities.label: Bahman
entities.summary: The son of Esfandiar, sent as messenger to Rostam; his father entrusts him to Rostam as he dies, and Rostam raises him.

entities.label: Nush-Azar
entities.summary: A son of Esfandiar, killed by Zavareh in the fighting beside the Hirmand.

entities.label: Mehrnush
entities.summary: A son of Esfandiar, brother of Nush-Azar, killed by Faramarz.

entities.label: Rostam
entities.summary: The great champion of Zabulistan, son of Zal, who will not go to the king in bonds.

entities.label: Zal
entities.summary: The father of Rostam, who counsels him to yield and, when Rostam is wounded, calls the Simorgh.

entities.label: Rudabeh
entities.summary: The mother of Rostam, who mourns when he comes home wounded.

entities.label: Zavareh
entities.summary: The brother of Rostam, who leads his men to the field and kills Nush-Azar.

entities.label: Faramarz
entities.summary: The son of Rostam, who kills Mehrnush.

entities.label: Simorgh
entities.summary: The great bird who heals Rostam and Rakhsh and shows Rostam the branch of tamarisk that is Esfandiar’s death.

facts.text: Helper of the house of Zal

entities.label: Rakhsh
entities.summary: Rostam’s horse, wounded by Esfandiar’s arrows and healed by the Simorgh.

entities.label: Iran
entities.summary: The kingdom of Goshtasp.

entities.label: Zabulistan
entities.summary: The land of Zal and Rostam, where Jamasp foretells Esfandiar will die.

entities.label: The Hirmand
entities.summary: The river of Zabulistan beside which Esfandiar camps and the two champions meet and fight.

entities.label: The arrow of tamarisk
entities.summary: The arrow Rostam makes from a tamarisk branch the Simorgh shows him, the only thing that can kill Esfandiar; he shoots it into Esfandiar’s eyes.

events.label: The poet’s spring
events.summary: The poet opens in spring, calling for wine, and hears the nightingale lament the death of Esfandiar.

events.label: Esfandiar asks for the crown
events.summary: Esfandiar comes home drunk and complains to his mother Katayun that the king keeps from him the crown he promised. Katayun tells Goshtasp, who asks Jamasp; the sage foretells that Esfandiar’s death lies in Zabulistan at the hand of Rostam.

events.label: Esfandiar reminds his father
events.summary: Before the court Esfandiar recounts what he did for the king: his years in chains in Gonbadan, the killing of Arjasp – and asks what excuse is left for withholding the crown.

events.label: The king’s condition
events.summary: Goshtasp answers that he sees no rival to his son but Rostam, who will not own the new king: Esfandiar must go to Sistan and bring Rostam back in bonds; then he shall have the crown. Esfandiar objects, but leaves in grief.

events.label: Katayun’s warning
events.summary: Katayun weeps and begs her son not to go to bind Rostam, the lord of sword and mace; he answers that he cannot disobey the king. She spends the night in tears.

entityAssociations.role: son who will not turn back

events.label: The ill omen of the camel
events.summary: At the parting of the roads the lead camel lies down and will not rise; Esfandiar has its head cut off to turn the omen back on it, and marches on to camp by the Hirmand. With Peshotan he resolves to send a messenger first.

events.label: Bahman sent to Zabulistan
events.summary: Esfandiar dresses his son Bahman in royal clothes and sends him with a message: Rostam has been ungrateful to the new kings and must come in bonds; Esfandiar promises to plead for him. Bahman crosses the Hirmand; Zal receives him and sends him to Rostam’s hunting ground.

events.label: Bahman at the hunting ground
events.summary: Bahman finds Rostam roasting an onager under a tree, a cup of wine in his hand. He rolls a stone down at him; Rostam stops it with his heel. Rostam welcomes him, and Bahman gives his father’s message.

events.label: Rostam’s answer
events.summary: Rostam answers Esfandiar that a wise man looks to the end of things: he will gladly come to him and to the king, but he will ask the king why his feet should be put in chains.

events.label: The meeting on the Hirmand
events.summary: Rostam orders a royal feast prepared, sends Zavareh and Faramarz to Zal, and rides unarmed to the Hirmand. The two champions meet and greet each other with praise; Rostam invites Esfandiar to his house, but will not accept the bonds.

events.label: The invitation not sent
events.summary: Esfandiar tells Peshotan that he will not go to Rostam’s hall nor call him to his own; Peshotan warns him, but Esfandiar holds to it. Rostam waits in vain and rides back angry.

events.label: The quarrel at the feast
events.summary: Rostam comes to Esfandiar’s camp and is angered to be seated on the left. Esfandiar calls Zal a demon’s child cast out and raised by the Simorgh; Rostam praises his lineage and recalls his deeds, the Mazandaran and the seven trials; Esfandiar boasts of his own wars for the faith and of the Brazen Hold. They test each other’s grip.

events.label: The pledge to fight
events.summary: At the noon feast Rostam again offers peace and gifts, and to go with Esfandiar to the king unbound. Esfandiar insists on the bonds and they agree to fight in the morning. At the tent door Rostam laments the house of the kings; Peshotan pleads for peace in vain.

events.label: Zal’s counsel
events.summary: Rostam calls for his arms. Zal begs him to yield rather than fight the king’s son; Rostam prays through the night.

events.label: The single combat
events.summary: At dawn the two meet alone on the Hirmand, agreeing that no one shall help either. Their spears, swords and maces break, and the horses and men are worn out.

events.label: The death of Nush-Azar and Mehrnush
events.summary: Zavareh brings Rostam’s men and the Iranians are attacked; Zavareh kills Nush-Azar and Faramarz kills Mehrnush, two sons of Esfandiar, who turns in anger on Rostam for breaking the pact.

events.label: Rostam wounded
events.summary: Esfandiar’s arrows pierce Rostam and Rakhsh; Rostam climbs a hill and asks for a truce for the night. Esfandiar grants it and mourns his sons, sure that Rostam will die of his wounds.

events.label: Rostam comes home wounded
events.summary: Rostam reaches his hall covered with wounds; Zavareh, Faramarz and Rudabeh weep. Zal resolves to call the Simorgh.

events.label: The Simorgh’s secret
events.summary: Zal burns a feather and the Simorgh comes. It draws out the arrows and heals Rostam and Rakhsh, then leads Rostam to the sea, to a tamarisk: Esfandiar’s life lies in that wood. Rostam cuts the branch and makes an arrow, warned that whoever sheds Esfandiar’s blood will suffer for it.

events.label: The last offer
events.summary: At dawn Rostam stands before Esfandiar again, healed. He asks pardon and offers his ancient treasures and to serve him, but Esfandiar insists on the bonds.

events.label: The arrow in the eyes
events.summary: Seeing that pleading is no use, Rostam prays, sets the arrow of tamarisk to his bow and shoots Esfandiar in the eyes; the brazen-bodied prince falls from his horse and speaks with Rostam a last time.

events.label: Esfandiar’s last will
events.summary: Dying, Esfandiar tells Rostam that the tamarisk was only a pretext, and entrusts his son Bahman to him to be raised. Zavareh warns that evil will come to Zabulistan from Bahman.

events.label: The iron coffin
events.summary: Rostam has an iron coffin made and sends Esfandiar’s body to Iran. The nobles rage, and Peshotan and Esfandiar’s sisters reproach Goshtasp, who sent his son to his death for the throne; Iran mourns for a year.

events.label: Bahman’s return
events.summary: Bahman stays in Zabulistan, where Rostam teaches him riding, feasting and kingship and loves him more than his own son; Rostam writes to Goshtasp asking pardon. Bahman returns to Iran, and the king, finding him wise, calls him Ardashir.
